purpose: Test whether changing non-reference noise channels explains weak suppression, while holding reference audio and speech field fixed
selection: first source_id in each of the six existing discovery speakers, independent of new model outputs
fixed_factors: speech waveform and its six-channel field
common scale for all conditions of each source

conditioned_12wave.source_signals: p_k=n/K+(q_k-mean(q))/sqrt(K), q_k independent random-phase surrogates of n; summed reference exactly n
conditioned_12wave.interpretation: physically renderable conditional finite-wave sound field; not a real recording or exact diffuse-field realization
conditioned_12wave.roundoff_policy: after verifying error<1e-10, set reference to analytic padded n to ensure identical PCM bytes

primary_contrast: conditioned_12wave minus original_point in enhanced SI-SDR; the noisy reference is bit-identical
screening_rule: A >=3dB primary difference in at least five of six speakers for each noise is an operational strong spatial-sensitivity signal, not a population significance test
confirmation_policy: If a material contrast is observed, freeze its interpretation then use eight new complete utterances excluded from the original24, with two new random seeds; same-speaker repetition must be disclosed
data_role: diagnostic discovery; not final method test
